name: Copia Power Monarch, Mason Valley
heading: 3. Copia Power Monarch, Mason Valley — 1,000 MW Proposed
brief: Copia Power is proposing a 1,000 MW data center development across approximately 505 acres north of Yerington in Lyon County’s Mason Valley. On August 6, 2026 , the Lyon County Board of County Commissioners approved a planned-unit-development zoning change by a 3–1 vote, with one abstention . The proposal encompasses up to 4.6 million square feet across eight two-story data center buildings, electrical infrastructure and supporting facilities.

name: Tract South Valley Technology Park
heading: 2. Tract South Valley Technology Park — 1,215 MW Ultimate Potential
brief: Tract markets its South Valley Technology Park in Storey County at 1,215 MW of eventual campus capacity across approximately 1,534 acres . Unlike many speculative land banks, a substantial first project is genuinely underway. Its affiliated builder Fleet Data Centers broke ground in May 2026 on a leased facility within the park near USA Parkway at the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center.

name: Tract Virginia Highlands
heading: 1. Tract Virginia Highlands — 2,500 MW Marketed Development Capacity
brief: Tract lists its Virginia Highlands Technology Park in Storey County at a potential 2,500 MW of future data center capacity, making it the largest single marketed development park with an explicit owner-published MW figure in this comparison. The 8,590-acre property sits between the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center and Virginia City Highlands and is divided into 11 parcels ranging from about 250 to 1,200 acres. Its industrial zoning supports future computing and energy infrastructure.

name: FirstLight Manchester
heading: 3. FirstLight Manchester — 2 MW Fully Built-Out Capacity, Operating
brief: At 77 Sundial Avenue in Manchester , FirstLight Fiber operates one of New Hampshire’s documented commercial colocation facilities. Independent industry directory Data Center Map lists 2 MW of fully built-out power and approximately 15,000 square feet of available white-space capacity. FirstLight’s own facility page specifies 14,400 square feet , a Tier 2-standard configuration, two utility power feeds, dual uninterruptible power supplies and a backup generator. The area figures are not necessari

name: Concord Locke Road
heading: 2. Concord Locke Road — Roughly 15 MW Proposed, Decision Deferred
brief: The City of Concord’s public application identifies a proposed 8,160-square-foot building at 52 Locke Road , including approximately 7,220 square feet of data center space , an office, garage and caretaker residence. Northpoint Engineering submitted the plan for landowner Granite Municipal Manufacturing & Sales. AI infrastructure company Levitate is providing the design and cooling approach.

name: Bow Merrimack Station
heading: 1. Bow Merrimack Station — 350 MW Grid Study, Data Center Not Confirmed
brief: The largest number attached to a possible New Hampshire data center concerns the retired Merrimack Station site in Bow . Owner Granite Shore Power requested a preliminary grid feasibility assessment involving Eversource and a potential 350 MW electrical connection . New Hampshire Bulletin’s September reporting and WMUR’s review of the filings established that the regulatory paperwork does not explicitly identify a data center or even definitively designate the proposed facility’s location.

name: QTS East Windsor
heading: 3. QTS East Windsor — 70 MW-Plus Campus, Operating and Expanding
brief: QTS Data Centers lists 70 MW-plus of critical power capacity at its East Windsor campus, located at 159 Princeton-Hightstown Road in Mercer County. The site already serves business-continuity and disaster-recovery customers in the Northeast corridor and has its own substation. QTS is proposing an additional data center building, but has not published a separately confirmed megawatt addition for that building.

name: Chirisa Piscataway
heading: 2. Chirisa Piscataway — 90 MW Planned for Two Buildings
brief: Chirisa Technology Parks markets a 20-acre campus in Piscataway, Middlesex County, with 90 MW of power associated with its PNJ-01 and PNJ-02 buildings. The plans involve repurposing an existing building shell and constructing a neighboring two-story data center. The developer identifies the site as reserved for 2027 delivery . That scheduling language does not establish that 90 MW is already energized.

name: DataOne and Nebius, Vineland
heading: 1. DataOne and Nebius, Vineland — 300 MW Under Construction
brief: The largest New Jersey data center campus in this comparison is being built at South Lincoln Avenue in Vineland , Cumberland County. Nebius says DataOne is developing and owning the facility while Nebius will operate its GPU and server infrastructure. Local reporting and municipal proceedings describe a 300 MW development linked to Nebius’s infrastructure agreement with Microsoft. That number refers to the campus’s planned scale, not to a measured 300 MW of live computing load.

name: Meta Los Lunas
heading: 3. Meta Los Lunas — 118 MW Estimated Operating IT Power
brief: Meta’s Los Lunas data center in Valencia County is the most mature large computing operation in this comparison. Opened in 2019, it has grown through successive expansions and now includes AI infrastructure. The campus is real and operational, although Meta has not published a directly comparable public megawatt figure for its current server load.

name: Project Jupiter, Doña Ana County
heading: 2. Project Jupiter, Doña Ana County — Up to 2.45 GW of Proposed Dedicated Generation
brief: Project Jupiter , developed by STACK Infrastructure and its construction partners for Oracle-related AI infrastructure near Santa Teresa, is already under construction. On October 22 , Clayco and Kiewit reported topping out the structural framework of an 855,000-square-foot portion of the site. The companies said work began in October 2025, while Oracle reported on October 23 that more than $994 million in contracts had been awarded to 30 New Mexico firms, of which over $160 million had been pai

name: E2B4 Roswell Information Park
heading: 1. E2B4 Roswell Information Park — 4,960 MW Planned Critical IT Load
brief: The biggest published critical IT-power ambition in New Mexico is at Roswell Information Park , proposed by infrastructure developer E2B4 . The company describes an ultimate plan for 20 data halls carrying 4,960 MW of critical computing load , supported by approximately 6,500 MW of net on-site electrical generation . It separately advertises a first phase of five halls and 1,240 MW of IT load , with an estimated $74.75 billion full-build development cost . These are the developer’s planning assu

name: Blockfusion Niagara Falls
heading: 3. Blockfusion Niagara Falls — 500 MW Grid Request, 300 MW AI Campus Plan
brief: In Niagara Falls, Blockfusion USA is converting its former power-plant campus at 5380 Frontier Avenue for liquid-cooled AI computing. Unlike projects supported only by land purchases or grid filings, Blockfusion has a signed anchor customer: on September 16 it announced a 15-year lease with CoreWeave , accompanied by an expansion agreement.

name: NYDIG / North Country Colocation Services, Massena
heading: 2. NYDIG / North Country Colocation Services, Massena — 635 MW Proposed
brief: North Country Colocation Services (NCCS) , an affiliate associated with NYDIG , wants to develop a roughly 1.5 million-square-foot, 635 MW data center across three buildings at the former Reynolds/Alcoa East industrial site near the St. Lawrence River. The proposal reached Massena’s Planning Board in May, with public meetings continuing through the summer and autumn. The total is a proposed future electrical demand , not proof that 635 MW of data halls are energized.

name: TeraWulf Lake Mariner, Barker
heading: 1. TeraWulf Lake Mariner, Barker — Up to 750 MW Gross Expansion Potential
brief: TeraWulf’s Lake Mariner Data Campus in Barker, Niagara County, is the most advanced large AI data center build in this comparison. Located on a former coal-plant property near Lake Ontario, it combines operating AI hosting capacity with construction of new high-density data halls. The company reported 102 MW of revenue-generating critical IT capacity after its CB-3 delivery in July and another 336 MW under construction in CB-4 and CB-5 as of its August 5 second-quarter update.

name: Triangle Innovation Point West, Chatham County
heading: 3. Triangle Innovation Point West, Chatham County — 750 MW Proposed
brief: ECO TIP West LLC is pursuing a 750 MW data center at Triangle Innovation Point West, a more than 400-acre heavy-industrial property near Moncure in southeastern Chatham County. The developer says it had spent more than $11 million pursuing the campus before county commissioners imposed a temporary data-center moratorium in February 2026. Its stated figure is a future electrical requirement, not a utility meter reading or proof of a fully approved 750 MW electrical connection.

name: Natelli Holdings, Vance County
heading: 2. Natelli Holdings, Vance County — 900 MW Proposed
brief: Natelli Holdings submitted a multi-phase plan for a 900 MW data center campus on approximately 529 acres near U.S. Highway 158 and Poplar Creek Road outside Henderson. The September 9 filing, compiled from county documents , describes up to 12 data center buildings totaling approximately 4 million square feet over four phases. Developer Tom Natelli has said his team completed substantial planning and has discussed grid service with Duke Energy. This is still a proposed project, not 900 MW of ope

name: Amazon Web Services, Richmond County
heading: 1. Amazon Web Services, Richmond County — Approximately 1,000 MW Reported Demand
brief: Amazon Web Services is constructing a $10 billion cloud and AI campus at the Energy Way Industrial Park near Hamlet in Richmond County. North Carolina announced the project in June 2025 , alongside a pledge of at least 500 permanent jobs . Amazon broke ground in October 2025, and public permit filings describe a large phased campus with approximately 20 to 21 buildings planned across several years. This is the most advanced new megascale data center development in the ranking.

name: Critical Data House Project Fighting Pike, Williston
heading: 3. Critical Data House Project Fighting Pike, Williston — 455 MW Planned, Delayed
brief: Critical Data House’s Project Fighting Pike is a proposed seven-building, 455 MW campus on approximately 300 acres near U.S. Highway 2 and 56th Street NW in Williston. The published development plan groups the buildings into three phases and includes utility areas, roads, stormwater ponds and security access. The developer has discussed up to $5 billion for construction and another $5 billion for computing equipment , figures that depend on the project actually proceeding.

name: Geronimo Power Harmony Energy Park, Cass County
heading: 2. Geronimo Power Harmony Energy Park, Cass County — 540 MW Proposed
brief: Geronimo Power submitted a conditional-use permit application on September 15, 2026 , for a data center on a 640-acre section of Harmony Township northeast of Casselton and north of Mapleton. Its proposal includes two main data center buildings , roads and related infrastructure. The developer says the initial utility service could reach 540 MW and that roughly 160 acres would contain buildings and improved surfaces, with more than three-quarters of the section remaining open land.

name: Atlas Power Data Center, Williston Area
heading: 1. Atlas Power Data Center, Williston Area — 700 MW Phased Development Plan
brief: Atlas Power’s existing computing complex west of Williston is the largest phased power ambition in this comparison. In a January 26, 2022 announcement , North Dakota’s governor described a $1.9 billion development on roughly 77 acres built by FX Solutions and served by Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative. The original schedule called for 240 MW in the first phase , a rise to 500 MW in the second, and an eventual 700 MW in the third. The project was designed chiefly for Bitcoin mining and oth

name: Cologix Johnstown Campus
heading: 3. Cologix Johnstown Campus — 800 MW Planned Full Buildout
brief: Cologix announced a new hyperscale and AI-ready campus in Johnstown, Licking County , after acquiring approximately 154 acres in November 2024. Its original company announcement describes a potential 800 MW across eight data center buildings and approximately 2 million square feet , with more than $7 billion in anticipated development spending. The 800 MW figure is a full-build opportunity, not evidence that eight buildings or all their substations are commissioned.

name: Meta Prometheus, New Albany
heading: 2. Meta Prometheus, New Albany — Gigawatt-Scale AI Supercluster, First Phase Operating
brief: Meta’s Prometheus facility in New Albany is substantially further along. In an October 19 engineering report , Meta said the first phase is complete and has already been used to train its Muse models. The company describes the installation as a gigawatt-scale AI supercluster , which is the basis for ranking its planned scale ahead of the 800 MW Johnstown development. It does not report a precisely metered 1,000 MW IT load currently operating.

name: PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, Piketon
heading: 1. PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, Piketon — 8 GW Planned IT Capacity
brief: The largest documented Ohio data center development is PORTS-Pike , the proposed AI campus at the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant near Piketon. In its August 17 announcement , OpenAI said it agreed to secure approximately 8 gigawatts of critical IT capacity from developer SB Energy . NVIDIA’s disclosed arrangement provides credit support for an initial 4.25 GW of land, power and building capacity, plus an option on the remaining 3.75 GW. SB Energy is to own and operate the development

name: Cloverleaf Project Open Sky, Piedmont
heading: 3. Cloverleaf Project Open Sky, Piedmont — About 1,400 MW Proposed
brief: Cloverleaf Infrastructure is pursuing a large campus on the north side of Piedmont in Canadian County. The company’s filing for its initial approximately 633-acre development describes six data center buildings , each approximately 352,800 square feet , along with a substation, warehouses, internal roads, landscaping and drainage facilities. An expanded footprint, including land options in nearby Kingfisher County, supports a long-range aim of around 1.4 GW of electricity demand . The first six-

name: Core Scientific Muskogee
heading: 2. Core Scientific Muskogee — 1,500 MW Planned Gross Power; Existing Capacity Secured
brief: Core Scientific has a materially different position in Muskogee: it owns or controls operational infrastructure and is constructing more high-density colocation space for AI customers. On August 14 , the company announced the completion of its approximately $444 million acquisition of Polaris DS , securing access to around 440 MW of existing gross, grid-connected power capacity under agreements with Oklahoma Gas & Electric. That electricity supply was already being used at the Polaris site, prin

name: Project Thunderbird, Enid
heading: 1. Project Thunderbird, Enid — Up to 2,750 MW of Planned IT Capacity
brief: Project Thunderbird is the largest announced Oklahoma development by its developer’s stated 2.75 GW of eventual critical IT capacity . Plainsmen Holdings, a group led by Enid business owners, proposes a four-campus data center corridor and related utility infrastructure covering approximately 1,735 acres at full buildout. Its model also envisions up to 3.3 GW of dedicated power generation . The 3.3 GW is a separate supply-side design envelope, not another 3.3 GW of server demand to add to the 2.
